This module applies two small fixes to teleprint when it loads. Each fix
checks whether the installed teleprint already has it and does nothing
if so. `FRAME_PATCHED` and `INK_PATCHED` are `True` when the module
applied the fix.

The first fix concerns rows already written to the scrollback. Teleprint
keeps a mark, `_ws`, of how many rows of the document it has committed
to the scrollback. Each frame writes only the rows past the mark. Those
rows are history in the terminal and cannot be taken back. When a tool
result folds, the document gets shorter. Teleprint used to lower the
mark to match, and the next frame wrote earlier rows a second time. A
session with many folded calls had many copies of its startup banner.
The fix never lets the mark go down.

The second fix adds a hook, `Compositor.on_frame`, which runs after each
paint. Pictures need the hook, because a picture is placed on the screen
after the text is drawn. The section on pictures below explains this.
The module installs the hook before the mark fix.
`Compositor._frame.__wrapped__` is therefore the frame without the mark
fix, and the test below uses it to show the duplicated rows.

``` python
from teleprint.testing import EmuTty as _EmuTty
```

``` python
async def _marks_over_a_fold(frame):
    "The ink mark after growth, after a fold, and after growing again, under `frame`."
    tty = _EmuTty(40, 8)
    comp = Compositor(tty); comp._register_signals = lambda: None
    await comp.start()
    comp.put('banner', Text('BANNER'), source='BANNER')
    tall = comp.put('tall', Text('\n'.join(f'line {i}' for i in range(20))), source='x')
    out = []
    frame(comp); out.append(comp._ws)
    tall.collapsed, tall.collapse_at = True, 1
    comp._dirty(tall); frame(comp); out.append(comp._ws)
    comp.put('again', Text('\n'.join(f'again {i}' for i in range(20))), source='y')
    frame(comp); out.append(comp._ws)
    tty.close()
    return out

_marks = await _marks_over_a_fold(Compositor._frame)
assert _marks[0] > 0, 'the document has to outgrow the window for anything to be inked at all'
test_eq(_marks, sorted(_marks))

if INK_PATCHED:
    _bare = await _marks_over_a_fold(Compositor._frame.__wrapped__)
    test_eq(_bare[1], 0)
    assert _bare != sorted(_bare)
```

``` python
_h_tty = _EmuTty(30, 6)
_h_comp = Compositor(_h_tty); _h_comp._register_signals = lambda: None
await _h_comp.start()
_fired = []
_h_comp.on_frame = lambda: _fired.append(_h_comp._cursor)
_h_comp.put('one', Text('one'))
test_eq(len(_fired), 1)
_h_comp.paused = True
_h_comp.put('two', Text('two'))
test_eq(len(_fired), 1)
_h_tty.close()
```

Ramabana gives `shift+enter` its own meaning: it starts a new line in
the composer, and plain `enter` sends. Leela’s terminal and a default
tmux never pass `shift+enter` on, so there it arrives as `enter` and
sends. By default a terminal sends the same byte for both keys, so the
program has to ask the terminal for richer key reports. There are two
protocols for this:

- Kitty’s keyboard protocol, with flag 1 (“disambiguate”), reports a
  modified key as `CSI code;mods u`. Ghostty and kitty support it.
- Xterm’s modifyOtherKeys, at level 1, reports it as
  `CSI 27;mods;code ~`. Tmux sends this form when its `extended-keys`
  option is on, and the kitty form when `extended-keys-format` is
  `csi-u`.

The compositor asks for both, and each terminal answers with the one it
supports.
[`ext_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#ext_key)
turns either report into the same `Key` the old byte parser would have
produced. Once kitty’s flag is on, `esc`, control letters and alt
letters also arrive in the new form. The decoder covers every key and
follows these rules:

- A key release is dropped.
- Keypad keys decode to the same characters and names the old bytes
  gave.
- `ctrl+i`, `ctrl+j` and `ctrl+m` stay `tab` and `enter`.
- Kitty’s other private-use keys, such as bare modifiers and media keys,
  are dropped rather than typed.
- Caps lock and num lock are ignored, since they are states rather than
  key chords.
- Super, the command key on a Mac, adds `mod+` to the name, which is
  Leela’s name for it, and never types a character: `cmd+a` decodes as
  `mod+a`.
- Chords with hyper or meta have no names here and are dropped.

[`ext_keys_ok`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#ext_keys_ok)
decides whether to ask. It returns `True` only when the compositor’s
terminal and standard output are both real terminals. Tests and pipes
never see the escape codes. The compositor turns the modes off wherever
it hands the terminal back: at `stop`, at `borrow` when another program
has the terminal, before a fatal signal, and while `ctrl+z` has the
process suspended. A `ctrl+z` from the transcript view also leaves the
alternate screen while suspended and returns on `fg`. Kitty keeps a
separate flag stack for the alternate screen. The transcript view sets
the flag again there and clears it before leaving.

def _ks(*chunks):
    p = Parser()
    return [e.name for c in chunks for e in p.feed(c)]
test_eq(_ks('\x1b[13;2u', '\x1b[27;2;13~', '\x1b\r', '\r'), ['shift+enter', 'shift+enter', 'alt+enter', 'enter'])
test_eq(_ks('\x1b[9;2u', '\x1b[27;2;9~', '\x1b[Z'), ['shift+tab'] * 3)
test_eq(_ks('\x1b[27u', '\x1b[99;5u', '\x03', '\x1b[49;3u', '\x1b1'), ['escape', 'ctrl+c', 'ctrl+c', 'alt+1', 'alt+1'])
test_eq(_ks('\x1b[13;2:3u', '\x1b[57428u'), [])
test_eq(_ks('\x1b[13;2', ':1u'), ['shift+enter'])
test_eq(Parser().feed('\x1b[97u'), [Key('a', 'a')])
test_eq(Parser().feed('\x1b[97;9u'), [Key('mod+a')])
test_eq(_ks('\x1b[97;10u', '\x1b[13;9u', '\x1b[97;17u'), ['mod+shift+a', 'mod+enter'])
test_eq(_ks('\x1b[57414u', '\x1b[106;5u', '\x1b[127;2u', '\x1b[57441u'), ['enter', 'enter', 'backspace'])
test_eq(ext_keys_ok(_EmuTty(10, 4)), False)
```

## Blocks and keys

Every block has a kind, and each kind has its own gutter, the mark in
the left margin. `GUTTERS` maps the nine kinds to their marks: `user`
for your prompts (`▌`), `step` for the agent’s narration (`┆`), `tool`
for a tool call (`│`), `reply` for the answer, `ask` for an approval
question (`◆`), `plan` for the plan checklist (`▸`),
[`note`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#note) for a
message from Ramabana itself (`·`), `error` (`×`), and `media` for a
picture.

A turn is one prompt and everything the agent does to answer it. In the
transcript a turn reads as a timeline in the order the work happened: a
`step` block for each stretch of narration, a `tool` block for each call
that narration introduced, and one `reply` block with the answer at the
end. A tool block folds to one summary row. Narration stays visible. The
answer always sits below the narration that led to it.

The cell below also defines the palettes. Each palette is a dict of
colour names (`bg0`, `fg1`, `red` and so on) to hex colours. `THEMES`
maps each theme name to its palette. `set_theme(name)` selects the
active palette. `auto` picks `light` or `github-dark` by the terminal’s
background: first the terminal’s answer to the `OSC11` query, then
`$COLORFGBG`, then `github-dark`. Every name in `THEMES` is a valid
`cli.theme` in config.toml, and
[`is_light`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#is_light)
says which palettes draw on a light background. `GRUVBOX` is a legacy
name that always holds the active palette, whatever its theme.
[`code_theme`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#code_theme),
[`hl_theme`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#hl_theme)
and [`code_bg`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#code_bg)
return the matching settings for highlighted code.
[`plan_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#plan_text)
draws the plan checklist in the active palette.

`auto` reads the terminal’s background in two ways. A terminal answers
the `OSC11` query with its colour as `rgb:RRRR/GGGG/BBBB`, and
[`reply_light`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#reply_light)
judges it by luminance. When no answer comes, `$COLORFGBG` names the
background as an ANSI colour number, where 7 and 9 to 15 are light.
Either test says None when it learns nothing, so the next one decides.
The palettes that `/theme` labels light are the ones whose `bg0` passes
the same luminance test:

``` python
test_eq([reply_light(b'\x1b]11;rgb:ffff/ffff/ffff\x1b\\'), reply_light('rgb:1a1a/1b1b/2626'), reply_light(b'')], [True, False, None])
test_eq([fgbg_light('0;15'), fgbg_light('15;default;0'), fgbg_light('')], [True, False, None])
[n for n in THEMES if is_light(n)]
```

### The key table

`KEYMAP` is the one list of what each key and typed command does. Each
row names an `action`, its `chords` in Leela’s notation (first one
first), a `label`, a `group`, the `CONTEXTS` it works in, and the `card`
line of the key card it belongs to; `command` marks typed text such as
`/peers` rather than keys. The key card (`HELP`, shown by `/help` and
`?`), the tips, the hint row’s key names and Sanketa’s keymap file are
all drawn from it, so they cannot drift from each other. The key
handlers keep their own code; a test checks that every chord in the
table is handled and every handled chord has a row.

`alt+enter` queues a line for after the turn. `shift+enter` starts a new
line in the message and never sends or queues, in terminals that report
it.
[`key_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#key_text)
writes a row’s keys the way the card does: a range as `alt+1..9`, a
shared modifier once, a bare arrow as `↑`.

Sanketa shows the keys of the app in front.
[`keymap_doc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#keymap_doc)
turns `KEYMAP` into its keymap file, format version 1: the app’s own
`app_version`, the rows without their `card` line, each label starting
with a capital, and no `overrides`, since ramabana’s keys cannot be
changed yet and Sanketa then shows them read-only.
[`write_keymap`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#write_keymap)
runs once at the start of a session. It writes `ramabana.json` into
`$SANKETA_KEYMAPS`, else into `~/.config/sanketa/keymaps` when
`~/.config/sanketa` exists, and nowhere when Sanketa is not set up. The
write goes through a temporary file in the same folder, because Sanketa
watches it; it is skipped when nothing but `written_at` would change (a
new `app_version` is a change), and when the file there was written by
another app. A failed write never stops the session.

## Attachments

A prompt can carry files: pictures, sound or text. In the terminal you
attach a file in one of three ways. You can drop the file on the window,
paste its path, or write `@path` in the prompt. All three make the same
attachment. The path parser accepts quoted paths, paths in brackets,
`file://` URIs and backslash-escaped spaces. It leaves a plain sentence
that mentions a path alone. The tests below check this.

A picture goes to the model as an image content part, the form a model
API takes images in. Every attachment also carries its absolute path.
The path works when the model cannot take the content part. A model
without audio support, for example, can open a `.wav` file through the
file tools.

The attachment helpers themselves,
[`media_paths`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/tools.html#media_paths),
[`Attachment`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/tools.html#attachment),
[`media_parts`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/tools.html#media_parts)
and the rest, live in `ramabana.tools` and are imported here so the
terminal and the other frontends share one parser.

### Pictures, drawn where the terminal can draw

A picture can reach the screen in two ways. The model can return one in
`Resp.media`. A tool can also write an image file during the turn and
report it through `on_media`. On a terminal without kitty graphics, the
picture is saved and its path is printed.
[`kitty_graphics`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#kitty_graphics)
decides which kind of terminal this is. It reads the environment
variables in `KITTY_ENV` and the `$TERM` substrings in `KITTY_TERM`, and
it accepts the `$TERM_PROGRAM` names in `KITTY_PROGRAM`. The `KITTY`
setting overrides all three.

On a terminal with kitty graphics the picture is drawn in place. Kitty
positions an image by screen cell, separately from the text. The
compositor redraws its document with absolute cursor moves. An image
cannot move with the text the way prose does. A
[`Picture`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#picture)
handles this in two steps.
[`Picture.send`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#picture.send)
transfers the image bytes to the terminal once. The block holds only the
blank rows the picture will cover.
[`img_cells`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#img_cells)
sizes them from
[`png_size`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#png_size).
[`Picture.place`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#picture.place)
then writes a short placement command at the end of every frame, at the
current position of those blank rows. Each placement reuses the
picture’s image id and replaces the previous placement. Repaints never
stack copies. Every frame places the picture again. A picture the
terminal cleared comes back on the next frame.

[`picture`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#picture)
builds a
[`Picture`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#picture) for
a file. It returns `None` when this terminal or this file cannot be
drawn. Only `.png` files can be drawn.
[`draw_png`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#draw_png)
is for code that has no frames to hook into. It sends and places a
picture at the cursor in one call.
[`media_line`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#media_line)
returns the transcript line for a saved picture.

Kitty also offers Unicode placeholders, which anchor the image to
special characters in the text. Ramabana does not use them. Kaku and at
least one other terminal ignore the `U=1` flag and draw at the cursor.
They print `U+10EEEE` as a missing glyph and leave a block of boxes
behind the picture.

### kitty_graphics

``` python
def kitty_graphics():
```

*Whether this terminal speaks the kitty graphics protocol.*

``` python
import os as _osr, struct as _struct, zlib as _zlib

def _a_png(w, h):
    "A real noise PNG, big enough to need several APC chunks."
    def chunk(tag, data):
        return (_struct.pack('>I', len(data)) + tag + data
                + _struct.pack('>I', _zlib.crc32(tag + data) & 0xffffffff))
    raw = b''.join(b'\x00' + _osr.urandom(3 * w) for _ in range(h))
    return (b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + chunk(b'IHDR', _struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0))
            + chunk(b'IDAT', _zlib.compress(raw)) + chunk(b'IEND', b''))
```

``` python
import os as _os
_seen = {k: _os.environ.pop(k, None) for k in (*KITTY_ENV, 'TERM', 'TERM_PROGRAM')}
try:
    test_eq(kitty_graphics(), False)
    test_eq(picture('/tmp/nope.png'), None)
    test_eq(draw_png('/tmp/nope.png'), '')

    import tempfile
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        png = b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + b'x'
        p = save_media({'mime': 'image/png', 'data': png}, d)
        test_eq(p.name, 'image-1.png')
        test_eq(p.read_bytes(), png)
        test_eq(p.parent.name, 'media')
        test_eq(save_media({'mime': 'image/png', 'data': png}, d).name, 'image-2.png')
        test_eq(save_media({'mime': 'image/avif', 'data': png}, d).suffix, '.avif')

    _os.environ['RAMABANA_KITTY'] = '1'
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        p = Path(d)/'a.png'
        p.write_bytes(_a_png(1200, 600))
        pic = picture(p, 24)
        test_eq((pic.cols, pic.rows), (24, 6))
        assert len(pic.send()) > 2 * APC_CHUNK
        test_eq(pic.send().count('m=0'), 1)
        assert 'a=t' in pic.send() and 'a=p' not in pic.send()
        test_eq(pic.place(), f'\x1b_Ga=p,i={pic.id},p=1,c=24,r=6,C=1,q=2\x1b\\')
        test_eq(len(pic.gap().plain.split('\n')), 6)
finally:
    _os.environ.pop('RAMABANA_KITTY', None)
    for k, v in _seen.items():
        if v is not None: _os.environ[k] = v
```

Text files can be attached too, up to `MAX_FILE_ATTACH` characters each.
A
[`FileAttachment`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#fileattachment)
captures the file’s text when you submit the prompt.
[`file_note`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#file_note)
adds the text of every attached file to the prompt, each tagged with its
exact path. The model reads the file as it was when you submitted the
prompt.
[`file_refs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#file_refs)
finds the `@path` references in a prompt.

[`steer_note`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#steer_note)
covers a line you send during a turn. That line reaches the model inside
a tool result, and a tool result cannot carry a picture. The note lists
each attachment by path. The model opens each one with `view_file`.

The cell after this one makes a few files to attach.

## The turn

A turn starts when you press enter on a prompt.
[`run_turn`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#run_turn)
runs one turn and streams it into the transcript. The agent’s stream is
a blocking generator. It runs on a separate model thread, and
[`run_turn`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#run_turn)
reads its chunks from a queue. The event loop stays free to handle
keystrokes, approval questions and activity updates while the model
works.

Some prompts get a row of choices before the turn starts. A request such
as “refactor the runtime” can mean “make the change”, “propose a plan”
or “say what is in scope”. Finding out afterwards which one the model
chose is costly.
[`options_for`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#options_for)
checks the typed line against the trigger words in `MENUS`. It returns a
title and a list of
[`Option`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#option)s, or
`None`.
[`ChoiceMenu`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#choicemenu)
draws the row above the input line and handles the keys that move
through it and pick one. Each
[`Option`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#option) has a
`suffix`, an instruction that the turn appends to your prompt. The model
receives the choice as part of what you asked for. `REFACTOR` is the
only menu. The examples of the menu in use come later, under the
surface.

[`close_done_shells`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#close_done_shells)
closes the tmux panes of `run_shell_bg` commands that have finished.
Their output stays readable through `cmd_output`.

Tool results and the files a turn changed are drawn in colour.
[`hl_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#hl_text)
highlights a piece of code in a given language.
[`diff_rich`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#diff_rich)
colours a diff. Both call [hl](04b_hl.ipynb) with the active palette and
the Lumis theme from
[`hl_theme`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#hl_theme).
In a unified diff, each line has the colour of an addition or a removal,
and the code inside is highlighted for the file’s language. A diffstat
has green and red bars. Any other text is gray.

[`changed_table`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#changed_table)
lists the files a turn wrote, with the largest change (lines added plus
lines removed) first. It shows at most `cap` files, 12 by default, then
a row that counts the remaining files, then a total row for every file.

[`opens`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#opens) decides
whether a finished call stays open. A file write stays open unless the
call’s `kind` is `run`. Any result that is a unified diff also stays
open. Other calls fold.
[`OpenDiff`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#opendiff)
wraps an open diff. It shows the first `DIFF_OPEN` lines and a hint
until you open the block.

## The message

The composer holds the message as a
[`MessageBuffer`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#messagebuffer).
It is a teleprint `Buffer` that also keeps a selection, from an anchor
to the cursor. `ctrl+a` and `mod+a` (Command on a Mac) select the whole
message. `shift` with an arrow, `home` or `end` extends the selection.
Typing or deleting replaces the selection, and a plain move ends it.
Assigning `text` clears the selection.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/cli.py#L1082"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

## The surface

[`Ui`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#ui) is the whole
terminal surface. The rest of this page builds on it. It has three jobs.
It paints the tail, the status bar and the input line at the bottom of
the screen. It turns tool calls and approval requests into blocks. It
decides what each keystroke means. `on_key` returns a coroutine for the
caller to start (a turn, for example), the string `'quit'`, or `None`
when the key was handled.

Every method on
[`Ui`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#ui) is
synchronous and does no terminal I/O of its own. The examples below
drive it against an emulated terminal with no mocks. Activity and
approval callbacks arrive on the model’s worker thread. Only the event
loop thread may touch the compositor. `_post` hands those callbacks to
the loop.

The class is long, and later cells add to it with fastcore’s `@patch`.
The methods a caller uses most are `submit` for the typed line, `say` to
print a block,
[`note`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#note) for a
one-line message, `stream` for reply text as it arrives, and `paint` to
redraw.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/cli.py#L1125"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Ui

``` python
def Ui(
    comp, agent, loop:NoneType=None
):
```

*The terminal surface: a transcript of blocks, a status bar, and one
line to type in.*

A line that starts with `/name` and is not one of the agent’s slash
commands is looked up as a skill or a command file. Command files are
markdown files in `<cfg>/commands/*.md`. When the `project_extensions`
option is on, they also come from a root’s `.agents/commands/`. For
example, `/exhash fix the loop` sends the prompt “fix the loop” with the
`exhash` skill attached. It does not report an unknown command. In a
command file, `$ARGUMENTS` is replaced by everything after the name,
`$1` to `$n` by its separate words, and each `@path` by that file when
the file lies inside the open folders. A command file with
`subtask: true` in its frontmatter is sent as a task for
`delegate_async`, which runs it in a sub-agent.

While an approval question waits, `y` approves and `n` refuses.
Lowercase `a` approves this request and every other request for the rest
of the session. Capital `A` approves and adds a rule that always allows
requests like this one. `always_allow` adds the rule when the approval
gate can hold rules, and
[`ask_pattern`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#ask_pattern)
is what the rule matches. Without rules, `A` behaves like `a`.
[`parse_answer`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#parse_answer)
reads a typed answer such as `y`, `no` or `n: put it in docs/`.

`ring` rings the terminal bell for a waiting question, but only when
nobody has typed for `BELL_IDLE` seconds (5). `nudge` shows the question
again every `REASK_EVERY` seconds (120) while it waits, and `reask` does
the showing. `#note TEXT` at the prompt calls `note_memory`, which keeps
the line for later sessions.

*`(ok, note)` for a typed approval answer (`y`, `n`, `n: reason`), or

``` python
from types import SimpleNamespace

class _QueueWork:
    def __init__(self): self.closed = False
    def close(self): self.closed = True

class _QueueTask:
    def add_done_callback(self, callback): self.callback = callback
    def done(self): return False

class _QueueComp:
    def __init__(self): self.blocks, self.started = {}, None
    def drop(self, *keys):
        for k in keys: self.blocks.pop(k)
    def spawn(self, work, name):
        self.started = work
        return _QueueTask()

class _QueueUi:
    agent = SimpleNamespace(leftovers=lambda: [])
    _echo, _retract, _replay = Ui._echo, Ui._retract, Ui._replay
    _turn_over, start_turn, _next_queued, take_back = Ui._turn_over, Ui.start_turn, Ui._next_queued, Ui.take_back
    _queued_prompt = Ui._queued_prompt
    flash, mark_read, kind = Ui.flash, Ui.mark_read, Ui.kind
    def __init__(self, turn=None):
        self.comp, self.turn = _QueueComp(), turn
        self._queued, self._queued_echo, self._echoed = None, [], []
        self._steered, self._queued_typed = [], ''
        self._steer_drafts = {}
        self._queued_text, self._typed, self._prompt, self._flash = [], '', None, None
        self.buf = SimpleNamespace(text='', cursor=0)
        self.notes, self.painted, self.attachments, self.kinds = [], False, [], {}
    def say(self, body, kind='reply', **kw):
        block = type('Block', (), {'key': len(self.comp.blocks) + 1, 'body': str(body)})()
        self.comp.blocks[block.key], self.kinds[block.key] = block, kind
        return block
    def note(self, text, kind='note'):
        self.notes.append((text, kind))
        return self.say(text, kind)
    def paint(self): self.painted = True

u = _QueueUi()
u._echo('now')
now = _QueueWork()
assert u.start_turn(now)
test_eq([(b.body, u.kind(b)) for b in u.comp.blocks.values()], [('now', 'user')])

u = _QueueUi('running')
u._echo('second')
second = _QueueWork()
assert not u.start_turn(second)
test_eq([(b.body, u.kind(b)) for b in u.comp.blocks.values()],
        [('queued · it runs when this turn ends · alt+up takes it back · ctrl+c stops this turn', 'note')])

u._echo('third')
third = _QueueWork()
assert not u.start_turn(third)
assert third.closed
assert all(b.body != 'third' for b in u.comp.blocks.values())
assert u._queued is second

u.turn = None
u._next_queued()
assert u.comp.started is second
assert u._queued is None
assert list(u.comp.blocks.values())[-1].body == 'second'

u = _QueueUi('running')
u._echo('/clear me')
u._typed = '/clear me'
clear = _QueueWork()
u.start_turn(clear)
assert u.take_back()
assert clear.closed and u._queued is None and u.buf.text == '/clear me', 'a queued command goes back as it was typed'
assert all(b.body != '/clear me' for b in u.comp.blocks.values())

u = _QueueUi('running')
u._echo('retry me')
retry = _QueueWork()
u.start_turn(retry)
u.turn = None
def fail_spawn(work, name): raise RuntimeError('busy')
u.comp.spawn = fail_spawn
u._next_queued()
assert u._queued is retry
assert all(b.body != 'retry me' for b in u.comp.blocks.values())
assert u.notes[-1] == ('the waiting message did not start: RuntimeError: busy', 'error')
```

``` python
class _SteerAgent:
    def __init__(self, listening=True): self.listening, self.told, self.left = listening, [], []
    def steer(self, text):
        if self.listening: self.told.append(text)
        return 'told' if self.listening else ''
    def leftovers(self): out, self.left = self.left, []; return out

_QueueUi.steer = Ui.steer
u = _QueueUi('running'); u.agent = _SteerAgent()
u._echo('look at b')
assert u.steer('look at b')
test_eq(u.agent.told, ['look at b'])
test_eq([b.body for b in u.comp.blocks.values()], ['↪ look at b'])
test_eq(u._flash[0], 'sent · read after the current call')

assert not _QueueUi(None).steer('no turn of ours')
u = _QueueUi('running'); u.agent = _SteerAgent(listening=False)
assert not u.steer('nobody listening') and u.agent.told == []

u = _QueueUi('running'); u.agent = _SteerAgent()
held = _QueueWork()
u.start_turn(held, prompt='queued line')
u.agent.left, u.turn = ['unread steer'], None
u._next_queued()
assert held.closed and u._queued is None
test_eq(u.comp.started.cr_frame.f_locals['prompt'], 'unread steer\n\nqueued line')
u.comp.started.close()
```

There are two ways to change the approval mode, one for each direction.
`tighten_approve`, bound to `ctrl+g`, makes approvals one step stricter,
from `auto` to `edits` to `ask` to `off`. It never loosens them.
Loosening takes a typed command. `approve_mode` handles `/approve MODE`,
which moves in either direction. `/approve` alone prints the current
mode.

### Ui.approve_mode

``` python
def approve_mode(
    want:str=''
):
```

*`/approve [off|ask|edits|auto]`, or the current mode when `want` is
empty.*

`cycle_approve`, bound to `shift+tab`, goes round `ask`, `edits` and
`auto`, then into plan mode. In plan mode every tool that acts on the
world is withheld and the model proposes a plan instead. The next press
leaves plan mode and goes back to `ask`. `off` is not on the cycle. From
`off`, the next press goes to `ask`.

`chip` returns the short label for plan mode or the current approval
mode. It returns `None` when no approvals gate the session. Every one of
these controls also answers a question that was already waiting.
Changing the mode to `auto` approves the request in front of you.

``` python
from ramabana.agent import Approvals
from ramabana.tools import WRITE_TOOLS

class _Planner:
    "Enough of an `Agent` for the approval controls: approvals, and plan mode."
    plan_mode = False
    def __init__(self, approvals): self.approvals = approvals
    def set_plan_mode(self, on): self.plan_mode = on; return on

class _Holder:
    "Enough of a `Ui` for the approval controls."
    def __init__(self, approvals): self.agent = _Planner(approvals)
    tighten_approve, approve_mode, cycle_approve, chip = Ui.tighten_approve, Ui.approve_mode, Ui.cycle_approve, Ui.chip

u = _Holder(Approvals(tools=WRITE_TOOLS, mode='auto'))
test_eq(u.tighten_approve(), 'approvals: auto -> edits')
test_eq(u.tighten_approve(), 'approvals: edits -> ask')
test_eq(u.tighten_approve(), 'approvals: ask -> off')
assert 'off' in u.tighten_approve()
test_eq(u.agent.approvals.mode, 'off')

test_eq(u.approve_mode(), 'approvals: off')
test_eq(u.approve_mode('ask'), 'approvals: off -> ask')
test_eq(u.approve_mode('yolo'), 'usage: /approve [off|ask|edits|auto]')
test_eq(u.agent.approvals.mode, 'ask')

test_eq(_Holder(None).tighten_approve(), 'this session runs without approvals')

said = [u.cycle_approve() for _ in range(3)]
test_eq(said[:2], ['approvals: ask -> edits', 'approvals: edits -> auto'])
assert said[2].startswith('plan mode') and u.agent.plan_mode and u.chip().plain == '⏸ plan'
test_eq(u.cycle_approve(), 'approvals: auto -> ask')
assert not u.agent.plan_mode
u.agent.approvals.mode = 'off'
test_eq(u.chip().plain, '⊘ off')
test_eq(u.cycle_approve(), 'approvals: off -> ask')
test_eq(_Holder(None).chip(), None)
```

### Shell lines

A line that starts with `!` runs as a shell command in the first open
folder, with no approval question, because you typed it yourself.
`run_shell_line` runs it. Its output prints as one block, followed by
the exit code, and a non-zero exit code prints as an error. The model
never sees the command or its output.

So that the model knows this exists,
[`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main) adds
`SHELL_NOTE` to an interactive session’s `extra_sp`, the extra text
appended to the agent’s briefing, before a resumed session builds its
briefing. The note tells the model it can ask you to run a command with
`!`. A one-turn run from the command line never gets the note.

The command runs in its own process group with stdin from `/dev/null`,
so a command that tries to read from the terminal gets end of file
instead of hanging. `Ui.shell_proc` holds the process while it runs,
which is how `ctrl+c` reaches it (see `stop` further down).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/cli.py#L2569"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Ui.run_shell_line

``` python
async def run_shell_line(
    command
):
```

*Run one owner-typed `!` line in the first open folder, printing its
output and exit code.*

``` python
sh_tty = EmuTty(72, 14)
sh_comp = Compositor(sh_tty)
sh_comp._register_signals = lambda: None
await sh_comp.start()
sh_ui = Ui(sh_comp, fake_agent(host=FullHost())[0])
sh_ui.buf.insert('!echo made > out.txt; cat out.txt; exit 3')
sh_ui.start_turn(sh_ui.submit())
await asyncio.wait_for(sh_ui.turn, 5)
sh_said = [sh_ui.transcript.block_text(b) for b in sh_comp.blocks.values()]
test_eq(sh_ui.turn, None)
assert (Path(sh_ui.agent.host.roots[0])/'out.txt').exists()
assert any('made' in s for s in sh_said) and any('exit 3' in s for s in sh_said)
sh_said
```

Replies are written in Markdown and drawn with Rich. `MARKDOWN_THEME`
gives headings, inline code, links and lists their own colours in the
active palette. The transcript keeps the text the model wrote as plain
Markdown. Only the drawing adds colour. Rich markup inside a reply, such
as `[red]`, appears as literal text. A reply cannot inject terminal
styling.

[`Ui.reply`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#ui.reply)
draws a reply. It uses
[`Reply`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#reply), which
is Rich’s `Markdown` with code blocks drawn by
[`ThemedCode`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#themedcode).
[`compact_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#compact_md)
joins plain paragraphs with single line breaks to save rows.
[`fence_lang`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#fence_lang)
maps a code fence’s language to the highlighter’s name for it.

The cell below uses the options row from the turn section.
[`options_for`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#options_for)
finds that “refactor the runtime” matches a menu.
[`ChoiceMenu.choose`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#choicemenu.choose)
takes one keystroke at a time and returns `(done, option)`.
[`Ui`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#ui) decides what
the chosen option means for the prompt. In the example, `down` moves the
cursor and `enter` picks “plan”.

``` python
menu = ChoiceMenu(*options_for('refactor the runtime'))
test_eq(menu.choose('down'), (False, None))
test_eq(menu.choose('enter')[1].label, 'plan')
test_eq(ChoiceMenu('x', REFACTOR).choose('s')[1].label, 'scope')
test_eq(ChoiceMenu('x', REFACTOR).choose('escape'), (True, None))
test_eq(options_for('what does the runtime do?'), None)
print('\n'.join(r.plain for r in menu.render()))
```

``` python
from rich.console import Console
color_console = Console(width=72, theme=MARKDOWN_THEME, color_system='truecolor')
styled = Markdown('# Heading\n\nUse `search_code` and **verify** it.\n\n```python\nanswer = 42\n```',
                  code_theme='github-dark')
lines = color_console.render_lines(styled, pad=False)
colors = {seg.style.color.triplet for line in lines for seg in line
          if seg.style and seg.style.color and seg.style.color.triplet}
inline = next(seg for line in lines for seg in line if seg.text == 'search_code')
test_eq(inline.style.bgcolor, None)
test_eq(len(colors) >= 3, True)
```

The rest of the examples on this page build a complete surface in the
notebook: an emulated terminal, a real compositor, and an agent from
[`fake_agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/testing.html#fake_agent)
whose model replies are scripted. Typing “refactor the runtime” and
pressing enter opens the options row on screen.

``` python
tty = EmuTty(72, 14)
comp = Compositor(tty)
comp._register_signals = lambda: None  # nbdev executes this async cell on a worker thread
await comp.start()
agent, be = fake_agent(replies=['`threshold` is in `ramabana/runtime.py`, and it caps the reserve.'], local_multimodal=True)
ui = Ui(comp, agent)
comp.on_key = ui.on_key
ui.paint()
print(tty.term.text())
```

``` python
ui.buf.insert('refactor the runtime')
test_eq(ui.submit(), None)
ui.paint()
assert 'a  apply' in tty.term.text() and 'p  plan' in tty.term.text()
test_eq(ui.menu.choose('escape'), (True, None))
ui.menu, ui.menu_prompt = None, ''
ui.buf.clear()
ui.paint()
```

Cancelling the menu, with `escape` or the `cancel` option, puts the line
back in the composer to edit instead of throwing it away.

``` python
ui.buf.insert('restructure the compactor')
ui.submit()
ui.on_key(Key('escape'))
test_eq(ui.buf.text, 'restructure the compactor')
ui.buf.clear()
ui.paint()
```

This is the resting state. The status bar shows the version, the model
and how full the context is, and the cursor sits on the input line.
Everything above the last two rows is the transcript.

``` python
[l for l in tty.term.text().splitlines() if 'tools' in l]
```

Typing goes through the real key parser: the example feeds the bytes a
terminal would send, not ready-made `Key` objects. Writing
`/search_code threshold` inside a prompt names a tool, which runs before
the turn starts.

``` python
comp.on_bytes(b'where is the threshold? /search_code threshold')
tty.term.text().splitlines()[-1]
```

While a turn runs, a working marker in the status bar moves on a timer.
The marker keeps moving during a silent wait on the network. With no
turn running, the status bar shows a steady ready dot.

``` python
resting_status = ui.status().plain
assert VERSION in resting_status
ui.turn = object()
first = ui.status().plain
ui.frame += 1
second = ui.status().plain
ui.turn = None
test_eq('● ' in resting_status and 'WORKING' not in resting_status, True)
test_eq('⠋ working' in first, True)
test_eq('⠙ working' in second, True)
```

Pressing enter prints the prompt as a `user` block and starts the turn.
The short `await` gives the model thread time to run. In the real app
the event loop does that waiting. Nothing blocks the screen.

``` python
comp.on_bytes(b'\r')
await asyncio.sleep(0.4)
print(tty.term.text())
```

``` python
ui.buf.text, ui.buf.cursor = 'x' * 80, 80
ui.paint()
test_eq(comp._cursor[1], len(ui.buf.text) % tty.size[0])
test_eq(0 <= comp._cursor[0] < comp.rows, True)
ui.buf.text, ui.buf.cursor = 'top\nbottom', len('top\nbottom')
ui.paint()
test_eq(comp._cursor[1], len('bottom'))
test_eq(0 <= comp._cursor[0] < comp.rows, True)
ui.buf.clear()
ui.paint()
```

`ctrl+p` and `ctrl+n` walk back and forward through the prompts you have
sent, and keep whatever you had half typed. `remember` stores each
submitted line and `recall` moves through them. With an empty composer,
`up` or `down` opens teleprint’s transcript view instead.

``` python
ui.buf.insert('first prompt')
ui.submit()
ui.buf.insert('second prompt')
ui.submit()
ui.buf.insert('unfinished draft')
ui.on_key(Key('ctrl+p'))
test_eq(ui.buf.text, 'second prompt')
ui.on_key(Key('ctrl+p'))
test_eq(ui.buf.text, 'first prompt')
ui.on_key(Key('ctrl+n'))
ui.on_key(Key('ctrl+n'))
test_eq(ui.buf.text, 'unfinished draft')
ui.buf.clear()
ui.on_key(Key('up'))
test_eq(ui.transcript.active, True)
ui.on_key(Key('g'))
test_eq(ui.transcript.top, 0)
ui.on_key(Key('escape'))
test_eq(ui.transcript.active, False)
```

The transcript now holds the prompt, the tool calls the agent made, and
the reply, each as a block with its own tag and height.

``` python
[(ui.kind(b), b.height) for b in comp.blocks.values()]
```

``` python
test_eq(agent.calls[0][0], 'search_code')
test_eq(any('threshold' in str(b.body) for b in comp.blocks.values()), True)
be.sent and len(be.sent)
```

## Folding

A block taller than `FOLD` (12 rows) starts folded. A four-hundred-line
result takes one row until you open it. `ctrl+o` opens all the working
of the latest turn, every step and call. A second press folds it again.
`alt+o` does the same for every turn. `alt+1` to `alt+9` open a single
entry, newest first. The main screen leaves the mouse to the terminal,
and selecting and copying work as in any scrollback. In the transcript
view, a block opens and closes under the block cursor or with a click.

``` python
long = ui.say(Text('\n'.join(f'line {i}' for i in range(40))), 'tool')
long.collapsed, long.height
```

``` python
comp.toggle(long.key)
test_eq(long.collapsed, False)
comp.toggle(long.key)
long.collapsed
```

A one-line block has nothing to fold, so toggling it does nothing and
raises no error.

``` python
short = ui.say(Text('one line'), 'tool')
comp.toggle(short.key), short.collapsed
```

A tool call folds to its own summary line. It does not wait for `FOLD`
rows. A turn of thirty calls reads as thirty lines, and you can open any
one result with a keystroke.

`_act` decides the fold when the result arrives. Ramabana prints a tool
block when the call starts, one row tall. When the call returns, it puts
the result into the same block. Teleprint’s `put` folds a block once,
when the block first grows past `collapse_at`. A call needs a different
rule. `_act` applies `_folded` again when the result arrives.

``` python
from ramabana.agent import Act
```

``` python
step = Act(tool='view_file', args={'path': 'runtime.py'}, summary='view runtime.py')
ui.on_act(step)
test_eq((ui.acts[step.id].height, ui.acts[step.id].collapsed), (1, False))

ui.on_act(step.finish('\n'.join(f'line {i}' for i in range(400))))
folded = ui.acts[step.id]
test_eq((folded.height, folded.collapsed), (401, True))
test_eq(len(comp._block_rows(folded)), 1)
assert step.summary in ui.transcript.block_text(folded)

comp.toggle(folded.key)
test_eq((folded.collapsed, len(comp._block_rows(folded))), (False, 401))
comp.toggle(folded.key)
```

The agent’s activity feed records each tool call as an
[`Act`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#act). Text the
model streams before a call is narration, so when a call starts,
`_close_seg` closes that text as a `step` block above the call. The
finished timeline stays on screen, and the reply block holds only the
text after the last call.

While the reply is still arriving its block is tagged `reply`. `/copy`
copies the final answer; the tool calls are the foldable trace above it.

``` python
tl_tty = EmuTty(72, 20)
tl_comp = Compositor(tl_tty)
tl_comp._register_signals = lambda: None
await tl_comp.start()
tl_agent, _ = fake_agent()
tl_ui = Ui(tl_comp, tl_agent)
tl_acts = tl_agent.activity

seg = tl_ui.stream(None, 'Looking for it.\n\nTwo places, probably.\n')
call = tl_acts.start('search_code', {'query': 'threshold'})
tl_acts.finish(call, 'runtime.py:88\nagent.py:12')
seg = tl_ui.stream(seg, '## Answer\n\nBoth of them.\n')
tl_ui.flush_stream()
tl_ui._seg_blk = None

timeline = list(tl_comp.blocks.values())
test_eq([tl_ui.kind(b) for b in timeline], ['step', 'tool', 'reply'])
test_eq([b.collapsed for b in timeline], [False, True, False])
test_eq(tl_ui.transcript.block_text(timeline[0]), 'Looking for it.\n\nTwo places, probably.')
test_eq(len(tl_comp._block_rows(timeline[1])), 1)
test_eq(tl_ui.transcript.block_text(timeline[-1]), '''## Answer

Both of them.
''')

status_tty = EmuTty(72, 10)
status_comp = Compositor(status_tty)
status_comp._register_signals = lambda: None
await status_comp.start()
status_agent, _ = fake_agent()
status_ui = Ui(status_comp, status_agent)
status_seg = status_ui.stream(None, 'Waiting for approval.\n')
status_ui.note('approved')
status_ui.stream(status_seg, 'Done.\n')
status_blocks = list(status_comp.blocks.values())
test_eq([status_ui.kind(b) for b in status_blocks], ['note', 'reply'])
test_eq(status_ui.transcript.block_text(status_blocks[-1]), 'Waiting for approval.\nDone.\n')
```

``` python
answer = timeline[-1]
test_eq(tl_ui.transcript.block_text(answer), '## Answer\n\nBoth of them.\n')
assert 'copied' in tl_ui.copy_last('reply')

test_eq(tl_ui.fold_work(), False)
test_eq([b.collapsed for b in timeline], [False, False, False])
test_eq(tl_ui.fold_work(), True)
test_eq([b.collapsed for b in timeline], [False, True, False])

class _FakePlan:
    def __init__(self): self.n = 0
    def md(self):
        rows = [f"{'[x]' if i < self.n else '[ ]'} step {i+1}" for i in range(3)]
        return f"**Repair**  \u00b7  {self.n}/3 done\n" + '\n'.join(rows)

plan_tty = EmuTty(72, 20)
plan_comp = Compositor(plan_tty)
plan_comp._register_signals = lambda: None
await plan_comp.start()
plan_agent, _ = fake_agent()
plan_ui = Ui(plan_comp, plan_agent)
plan_ui._plan_blk = None
_p, _blk = _FakePlan(), None
for _i in range(3):
    _p.n = _i
    plan_ui.on_plan(_p)
    _blk = plan_ui.stream(_blk, f'step {_i+1}\n')
plan_ui.flush_stream()
_plans = [b for b in plan_comp.blocks.values() if plan_ui.kind(b) == 'plan']
test_eq(len(_plans), 1)
assert '2/3 done' in plan_ui.transcript.block_text(_plans[0])

_md = ('**Repair**  \u00b7  1/2 done\n'
       '[x] `aaa` did the thing  -- with a note\n'
       '[ ] `bbb` still to do')
_t = plan_text(_md)
test_eq(_t.plain.splitlines()[1], '[x] aaa did the thing  -- with a note')
_styles = {_md_line: None for _md_line in ()}
_mark = [sp for sp in _t.spans if _t.plain[sp.start:sp.end] in ('[x]', '[ ]')]
test_eq(len(_mark), 2)
test_eq(len({sp.style for sp in _mark}), 1)
_step = next(sp for sp in _t.spans if _t.plain[sp.start:sp.end].strip() == 'did the thing')
assert _step.style != _mark[0].style
set_theme('dark');  _d = plan_text('[x] `a` x').spans[0].style
set_theme('light'); _l = plan_text('[x] `a` x').spans[0].style
assert _d != _l
set_theme('dark')
```

``` python
tl_ui._turn_at, tl_ui.turn = time.monotonic(), 'a turn'
footer = [r.plain for r in tl_ui.working()]
test_eq(footer[0], f'1 {call.line()}')
test_eq(tl_ui.drillable(), [tl_ui.acts[call.id]])
assert footer[-1].startswith('  step 1 ·'), footer
tl_ui.turn = None
test_eq(tl_ui.working(), [])
```

A delegation is a call where the agent hands a question to a sub-agent.
It shows as one entry with the sub-agent’s calls grouped under it. A
sub-agent is a second agent that the main agent starts for a piece of
work, here through `delegate_search`. It uses the same recorded tool
wrappers as its caller, and its calls arrive in the same
[`Activity`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#activity)
feed. Each call has a `parent_action_id`.
[`Agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent) sets
it from a per-thread stack of the delegate calls in flight.
[`Ui`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#ui) uses it to
put the call under its parent. Without the grouping, the calls of
several sub-agents would appear among the caller’s own calls.

`_folded` decides whether a call folds. A finished call that succeeded
folds to its summary when it has sub-agent calls or when
[`opens`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#opens) is
false for it (see above). A failed call never folds. A running call
folds only while `FOLD_RUNNING` is `True` and the call has no sub-agent
calls. `drillable` lists the turn’s foldable calls, newest first.
`drill(n)` opens or folds the `n`th of them. `alt+1` to `alt+9` call
`drill`.

``` python
parent = tl_acts.start('delegate_search', {'question': 'who reads the threshold?'})
for q in ('threshold callers', 'reserve usage'):
    tl_acts.finish(tl_acts.start('search_code', {'query': q}, parent_action_id=parent.id), 'hits')
tl_acts.finish(parent, 'Three callers, all in runtime.py.')

group = tl_ui.acts[parent.id]
test_eq(len(tl_comp.blocks), 4)
test_eq((group.collapsed, len(tl_comp._block_rows(group))), (True, 1))
assert '2 calls' in tl_comp._ansi(tl_comp._block_rows(group)[0][1])
assert all(k.line() in tl_ui.transcript.block_text(group) for k in tl_ui.kids[parent.id])

failed = tl_acts.start('run_shell', {'command': 'pytest'})
tl_acts.finish(failed, 'FAILED test_reserve\nassert 0.9 <= 0.8', ok=False)
test_eq(tl_ui.acts[failed.id].collapsed, False)
```

``` python
test_eq([tl_ui.kind(b) for b in tl_ui.drillable()], ['tool', 'tool', 'tool'])
test_eq(tl_ui.drill(2), True)
test_eq(group.collapsed, False)
test_eq(tl_ui.drill(2), True)
test_eq((group.collapsed, tl_ui.drill(99)), (True, False))

tl_ui.copy_last('turn')
test_eq(tl_ui._reply, '## Answer\n\nBoth of them.\n')

test_eq(tl_ui.mouse, False)
tl_ui.set_mouse('on')
test_eq(tl_ui.mouse, True)
tl_ui.leave_transcript()
test_eq(tl_ui.mouse, True)
tl_ui.set_mouse('off')
test_eq(tl_ui.mouse, False)
```

## Copying and browsing

There are two ways to copy out of the transcript, and both use the
system clipboard. On the main screen the mouse belongs to the terminal.
You select and copy as in any scrollback. The transcript view, opened
with `ctrl+r` or `up`, takes the mouse only while it is open
(`enter_transcript` and `leave_transcript`). `/copy` and the view’s `y`
key send the text over OSC 52, a terminal escape code for setting the
clipboard, which works through ssh and tmux.

`/copy` and the `y` key copy a block’s source text, not what is drawn.
The source is the Markdown the model wrote, or the arguments a tool got.
Text taken off the screen would be wrapped at the terminal’s width,
indented by the gutter and missing the code fences. Every block
therefore records its source when it is printed. `transcript.block_text`
returns it, as the examples show.

The last three examples attach files: `attach` adds a picture once and
refuses a duplicate, `paste` turns a pasted path into an attachment, and
`submit` sends the attachments with the prompt and clears them.

``` python
md = 'Here is the fix.\n\n```python\nthreshold = 42\n```\n\nCall it from `runtime.py`.'
rblk = ui.stream(None, md[:20])
rblk = ui.stream(rblk, md[20:])
test_eq(ui.transcript.block_text(rblk), md)
rendered = '\n'.join(''.join(s.text for s in l) for l in comp._content_lines(rblk))
assert '```' not in rendered
assert '```python' in ui.transcript.block_text(rblk)
```

``` python
u = ui.say(Text('where is the threshold?'), 'user')
test_eq(ui.transcript.block_text(u), 'where is the threshold?')
wrapped = ui.say('x' * 200, 'note')
test_eq(ui.transcript.block_text(wrapped), 'x' * 200)
test_eq(wrapped.height > 1, True)
ui.copy_last('reply')
```

``` python
ui.enter_transcript()
test_eq((ui.transcript.active, ui.transcript.follow), (True, True))
ui.say(Text('search_code("threshold") landed while browsing'), 'tool')
assert 'landed while browsing' in tty.term.text()
sblk = ui.stream(None, 'and a reply streamed ')
sblk = ui.stream(sblk, 'in behind it')
ui.touch(now=True)
assert 'in behind it' in tty.term.text()
ui.transcript.move(-1)
test_eq(ui.transcript.follow, False)
ui.leave_transcript()
test_eq((ui.transcript.active, comp.paused), (False, False))
```

``` python
ui.attach(shot); ui.attach(shot); ui.attach(snd_path)
test_eq([a.name for a in ui.attachments], ['shot.png', 'note.wav'])
assert 'shot.png' in ui.attach_row().plain
ui.detach('2')
test_eq([a.name for a in ui.attachments], ['shot.png'])
ui.detach(); ui.detach()
ui.attach(media_dir / 'gone.png')
test_eq(len(ui.attachments), 0)
test_eq(ui.attach_row(), None)
```

``` python
ui.paste(str(shot))
test_eq([a.name for a in ui.attachments], ['shot.png'])
test_eq(ui.buf.text, '')
ui.paste('and this is ordinary text')
test_eq(ui.buf.text, 'and this is ordinary text')
long_text = 'copied text ' * 100 + 'image.png'
ui.paste(long_text)
test_eq(ui.buf.text, 'and this is ordinary text' + long_text)
ui.buf.clear()
```

``` python
ui.buf.insert('what is in this picture?')
await ui.submit()
test_eq(ui.attachments, [])
```

## Approvals in a terminal

An approval is the question Ramabana asks before a tool with an effect
runs: a file write, a shell command, a git commit and so on. The
approval gate,
[`Approvals`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#approvals),
holds the model’s worker thread until a person answers. The request
arrives on that thread and the answer comes from the event loop thread.
While a question waits, the input line is where you answer it: `y`, `n`,
`a` for the rest of the session, or `n:` followed by a reason.

Here a write is requested from another thread, the way a tool call does
it:

``` python
tty2 = EmuTty(72, 12)
comp2 = Compositor(tty2)
comp2._register_signals = lambda: None
await comp2.start()
gated, _ = fake_agent(replies=['done'])
gated.approvals = Approvals(tools=WRITE_TOOLS, host=gated.host)
ui2 = Ui(comp2, gated)
comp2.on_key = ui2.on_key
ui2.paint()
threading.Thread(target=lambda: gated.approvals.request(
    'create_file', {'path': '/proj/notes.md', 'text': '# notes\n'}), daemon=True).start()
await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
print(tty2.term.text())
```

The question block shows what you need to decide: the path, whether the
write overwrites a file, and the start of what would be written. The
input line now holds the approval question.

``` python
test_eq(ui2.ask.tool, 'create_file')
tty2.term.text().splitlines()[-1]
```

[`parse_answer`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#parse_answer)
reads a typed answer. A line that is not an answer, such as a prompt
typed at the wrong moment, does not count as a refusal. The question is
shown again with a hint and keeps waiting. A waiting question also shows
itself again every `REASK_EVERY` seconds.

``` python
test_eq([parse_answer(t) for t in ('y', 'YES', 'n', 'no: too broad', 'n:', 'continue.', 'y: and add a test', 'approve', 'deny', 'ok')],
        [(True, ''), (True, ''), (False, ''), (False, 'too broad'), (False, ''), None, (True, 'and add a test'), (True, ''), (False, ''), None])

ui2.buf.insert('continue.')
ui2.on_key(Key('enter'))
assert ui2.ask is not None and ui2.ask.pending
test_eq(ui2.buf.text, '')

rang = []
_write = tty2.write
tty2.write = lambda s: rang.append(s) if s == '\a' else _write(s)
ui2._asked_at -= REASK_EVERY; ui2._key_at -= BELL_IDLE + 1
test_eq(ui2.nudge(), True)
test_eq(rang, ['\a'])
test_eq(ui2.nudge(), False)

ui2.buf.insert('n: beca')
ui2._asked_at -= REASK_EVERY; ui2._key_at = time.monotonic()
test_eq(ui2.nudge(), False)
test_eq((ui2.buf.text, rang), ('n: beca', ['\a']))
ui2._asked_at -= REASK_EVERY; ui2._key_at -= BELL_IDLE + 1
test_eq(ui2.nudge(), False)
test_eq((ui2.buf.text, rang), ('n: beca', ['\a', '\a']))
ui2.buf.clear()
tty2.write = _write
```

The question takes the input line, so what you type is read as the
answer and never sent to the model.

`y` and `a` answer at once when nothing has been typed. `n` waits for
enter, and a reason can follow it. `n` and enter refuses.
`n: put it in docs/ instead` refuses with that reason, and the model
receives the reason instead of the word “denied”.

``` python
comp2.on_bytes(b'n: put it in docs/ instead')
tty2.term.text().splitlines()[-1]
```

``` python
comp2.on_bytes(b'\r')
await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
ui2.ask, gated.approvals.history[-1].reply()
```

There are two histories, kept apart. The composer keeps your past
prompts, and teleprint’s blocks are the history of the transcript. `up`
and `down` recall a past prompt only when the cursor cannot move further
inside a prompt of several lines. `ctrl+r` opens teleprint’s transcript
view, where you can search old blocks, open them and copy them.

``` python
test_eq(bool(gated.approvals.history[-1]), False)
test_eq(tty2.term.text().splitlines()[-1], '▌')
[ui2.kind(b) for b in comp2.blocks.values()][-2:]
```

`a` approves the current request and sets the approval mode to `auto`
for the rest of the session.

``` python
threading.Thread(target=lambda: gated.approvals.request('create_file', {'path': '/proj/b.md'}), daemon=True).start()
await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
comp2.on_bytes(b'a')
await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
gated.approvals.mode, gated.approvals.history[-1].note
```

## Commands

The agent answers slash commands such as `/model`, `/tools` and `/cost`.
The terminal does not. Each command has one implementation, and every
frontend shares it. The terminal answers `/help` itself, because the
keys it describes belong to the terminal. An unknown command prints an
error block.

``` python
ui.buf.insert('/tools')
ui.submit()
[l for l in str(comp.blocks[max(comp.blocks)].body[0]).splitlines()[:4]]
```

``` python
ui.buf.insert('/nope')
test_eq(ui.submit(), None)
ui.kind(comp.blocks[max(comp.blocks)])
```

Commands are recognised before the options row, so `/tools refactor`
runs the command and opens no menu.

``` python
ui.buf.insert('/tools refactor')
test_eq(ui.submit(), None)
test_eq(ui.menu, None)
ui.kind(comp.blocks[max(comp.blocks)])
```

An empty line does nothing; no empty turn goes to the model.

``` python
test_eq(ui.submit(), None)
ui.buf.text
```

## Running it

[`mk_agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#mk_agent)
from `ramabana.agent` builds what the terminal runs. It makes a
[`WorkspaceHost`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/vault.html#workspacehost)
over the folders named on the command line, an
[`Agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent) over
that host, and an approval gate connected to both. A host is the object
that supplies the agent’s tools and decides what they may touch: which
folders, whether the network is reachable, and which writes need
approval.
[`mk_host`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#mk_host)
builds the host alone.
[`amain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#amain) is the
terminal loop that runs the
[`Ui`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#ui).

The prompt appears before the model is ready. `begin` builds the system
prompt and tools and starts the model on a thread. The status bar says
`starting model…` until the model is ready. A line sent before the model
is up waits in the queue, like a line sent during a turn. It runs when
the model is ready.

[`start_agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#start_agent)
starts the turn model and then the code index, the search index behind
`search_code`. The index never delays the model.
[`sync_index`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#sync_index)
decides whether the index needs rebuilding. It rebuilds when a package
or an open folder changed since the last good build. Otherwise it
reopens the saved index. It logs which one it did to `<cfg>/kosha.log`.
`warm_up` runs
[`start_agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#start_agent)
off the loop with
[`off_loop`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#off_loop).
It prints a note that gives the reason when no model starts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/cli.py#L2705"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Ui.begin

``` python
def begin():
```

*Start the model behind the prompt; lines sent meanwhile wait in the
queue.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/cli.py#L2694"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Ui.warm_up

``` python
async def warm_up():
```

*Start the model off the loop; a start that fails says why in a note.*

[`amain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#amain) is the
interactive loop. It uses one terminal, one event loop and one owner of
the keyboard. It starts the compositor and connects keys, pastes,
resizes and mouse events to the
[`Ui`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#ui). It starts
the model with `begin`. On exit it restores the terminal and shuts down
the agent.

Three helpers keep a broken terminal from breaking the session.
[`AppTty`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#apptty) is
teleprint’s `RealTty` with two changes. A write waits for a full
terminal to drain and sends the whole frame. When the terminal hangs up,
reading stops and writes are dropped, and the session quits instead of
spinning.
[`loop_error`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#loop_error)
shows an exception from a key handler or a posted notice as an error in
the session.
[`stderr_to`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#stderr_to)
sends Python’s stderr to a file while the screen belongs to the
compositor. A warning written straight to the terminal would scroll the
transcript under the compositor’s frames.
[`stderr_to`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#stderr_to)
also points `faulthandler` at that file, and a hard crash leaves its
stack trace there.
[`stderr_log`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#stderr_log)
names the file, inside the session’s own run folder.

For `--resume`,
[`pick_session`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#pick_session)
lists the newest saved sessions and asks which to open. `show_resumed`
draws the last `RESUME_SHOWN` turns of the reopened session before the
first prompt.

### AppTty

``` python
def AppTty():
```

*`RealTty` that waits out a full terminal, and stops reading and drops
writes once it hangs up.*

A terminal that another process left non-blocking takes only part of a
large frame. It then refuses the next write until it drains.
[`AppTty`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#apptty) waits
for it and writes the rest. Only a real hangup marks the terminal gone.
A gone terminal freezes the screen and quits the session on the next
key:

``` python
import pty, types
def _drain(m, got, n):
    while sum(map(len, got)) < n: got.append(os.read(m, 1 << 16))

def _pty():
    m, s = pty.openpty()
    a = termios.tcgetattr(s); a[1] &= ~termios.OPOST; termios.tcsetattr(s, termios.TCSANOW, a)
    os.set_blocking(s, False)
    t = object.__new__(AppTty); t.fd = s
    return m, s, t

out, wait = sys.__stdout__, WRITE_WAIT
m, s, t = _pty()
sys.__stdout__ = types.SimpleNamespace(fileno=lambda: s, flush=lambda: None)
try:
    got = []
    th = threading.Thread(target=_drain, args=(m, got, 400_000), daemon=True); th.start()
    t.write(b'a' * 200_000); t.write('b' * 200_000)
    th.join(5)
    assert not (t.gone or t.dropped)
    test_eq(b''.join(got), b'a' * 200_000 + b'b' * 200_000)
    test_eq(t.read(timeout=0), b'')
    assert not t.gone
    WRITE_WAIT = 0.05
    t.write(b'x' * 200_000); t.write(b'y' * 200_000)
    assert t.dropped and not t.gone
    os.close(m)
    t.write(b'after the hangup')
    assert t.gone
finally: sys.__stdout__, WRITE_WAIT = out, wait
os.close(s)
```

An exception from a key handler or a notice posted from another thread
reaches the event loop’s exception handler, which shows it as an error
and leaves the session running:

``` python
import io
class _Ui:
    closed, painted, notes = False, 0, []
    def note(self, text, kind='note'): self.notes.append((text, kind))
    def paint(self): self.painted += 1

async def _raises():
    u, loop = _Ui(), asyncio.get_running_loop()
    loop.set_exception_handler(loop_error(u))
    def bad(): raise ValueError('a key handler broke')
    loop.call_soon(bad)
    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    loop.set_exception_handler(None)
    return u

with contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()) as err: u = await _raises()
test_eq(u.notes[0][1], 'error')
assert 'a key handler broke' in u.notes[0][0] and u.painted == 1 and 'a key handler broke' in err.getvalue()
```

`read_outside` and `vault` stay off in the function signature. The
positive flags remain available to scripts that do not read
`config.toml`. The check below reads the exported entry point.

``` python
import inspect
import ramabana.cli as _cli_defaults
from fastcore.script import anno_parser
```

The parser keeps the positive flags available while both function
defaults stay off:

``` python
_signature_defaults = inspect.signature(_cli_defaults.main.__wrapped__).parameters
assert _signature_defaults['read_outside'].default is False
assert _signature_defaults['vault'].default is False
_script_flags = anno_parser(_cli_defaults.main.__wrapped__, pos=['prompt']).parse_args(['--read-outside', 'x'])
test_eq((_script_flags.read_outside, _script_flags.prompt), (True, 'x'))
(_script_flags.read_outside, _script_flags.vault)
```

The agent the terminal gets is a real one, over real folders, with
writes behind the approval gate. `approve='none'` builds it with no gate
at all:

``` python
tempdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
cli_agent, cli_host = mk_agent([tempdir], approve='ask', web=False)
cli_host.roots, sorted(WRITE_TOOLS & set(t.__name__ for t in cli_agent.tools))
```

``` python
test_eq(cli_agent.approvals.mode, 'ask')
test_eq(cli_agent.approvals.timeout, None)
test_eq(mk_agent([tempdir], approve='none')[0].approvals, None)
cli_agent.routing.name_for()
```

Without a terminal, `ramabana` runs one turn, which suits a pipe or a
script. [`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main)
is the entry point behind the `ramabana` command. It parses the options,
builds the agent with
[`mk_agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#mk_agent),
and then either runs one turn with
[`ask_once`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#ask_once)
or starts the interactive session with
[`amain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#amain).
[`headless_prompt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#headless_prompt)
picks the one-turn prompt: the argument, or stdin when the argument is
`-` or empty and stdin is a pipe.
[`host_kw`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#host_kw)
holds the host options the terminal adds. Outside tmux, an interactive
session first starts itself again inside a tmux server of Ramabana’s
own, as [setup](19_setup.ipynb) explains.

### main

``` python
def main(
    prompt:str='', # one turn and exit; omit for interactive
    root:str='.', # comma-separated folders: .,~/notes,/srv/app
    model:str=None, # turn model; omit for the routing default
    approve:str='ask', # ask | edits | auto | off | none (no gate)
    web:bool=True, # --no-web takes the web tools offline
    read_outside:bool=False, # reads reach any path; writes need --root
    subagent_writes:bool=True, # --no-subagent-writes restricts delegates to read-only tools
    vault:bool=False, # vishalakshi vault for reads
    pii:str='off', # off | redact | refuse PII from the vault, and from shell, Python and web reads a hosted model gets
    pii_ner:bool=False, # --pii also gates titled names
    spec:bool=False, # enable OpenAPI, Azure and Google Discovery tools
    theme:str='auto', # auto follows the terminal's background; /theme lists the palettes
    max_tool_calls:str='auto', # auto | 20..400 tool calls per turn
    max_steps:str='auto', # auto | 8..80 model/tool-loop steps per turn
    max_cost:float=None, # stop the turn once it has cost this many dollars
    cfg:str='~/.config/ramabana', # config dir: skills, extensions, resumable history
    resume:str='', # saved session id/prefix, or 'latest'; bare --resume lists this folder's sessions to pick from
    all_folders:bool=False, # with a bare --resume, list sessions from every folder
    json:bool=False, # with a prompt: print the full result as JSON
    bell:bool=True, # --no-bell silences turn-end and approval bells
    hints:bool=True, # --no-hints hides the row of keys under the status bar
    tips:bool=True, # --no-tips hides the tip under the working rows
    tmux:str='auto', # auto | on | off: read and run in tmux panes
    pane:str='auto', # auto | on | off: the `now` pane; auto in tmux
    doctor:bool=False, # check tmux and the now pane, offer to install tmux, and exit
    warm:bool=False, # seed a fresh session with dhrona's example rounds
    no_warm:bool=False, # start without them, which is the default
    no_read_outside:bool=False, # --no-read-outside turns off reads outside the folders even when config.toml turns them on
    no_vault:bool=False, # --no-vault turns off the vault even when config.toml turns it on
    optin:str='', # opt-in tool groups: exhash,research,author
    profile:str='auto', # auto | small | full: small suits ≤32k local models
    learned:bool=True, # --no-learned starts without <cfg>/learned, the lessons Dhrona keeps
):
```

*Run Ramabana as a terminal agent. Name every folder it may work on:
–root .,~/notes*

[`ask_once`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#ask_once)
runs the turn, prints the answer on stdout and any problems on stderr,
and returns the exit code. The exit code is 0, or 1 when the turn model
was not available. The answer on stdout works in a pipe, as in
`ramabana 'what changed?' | less`. With `as_json=True`, the `--json`
option, it prints the reply, usage, changed files, activity, problems
and session id as one JSON object.

``` python
piped, _ = fake_agent(replies=['nothing changed since the last commit.'])
test_eq(ask_once(piped, 'what changed?'), 0)
piped.note
```

The prompt is the one positional argument.
`ramabana 'which files import fastllm?'` runs one turn and exits. A bare
`--resume` lists this folder’s saved sessions and asks which to reopen,
through
[`pick_session`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#pick_session).

A session over this repository, on a local model, with nothing gated:

``` bash
ramabana --root . --model qwen-4b --approve none
```

A session that may read the rest of the machine but writes only here:

``` bash
ramabana --root . --read-outside
```

One turn for a pipe, with no terminal at all:

``` bash
ramabana 'which files import fastllm?'
```

`attach_file` attaches one text or notebook file. The file must be
readable under the host’s file policy and inside the open folders. A
picture or sound file goes to `attach` instead. Typing `@` in the prompt
offers file completion from the open folders, in the same tab menu that
completes slash commands, and when the prompt is sent,
[`run_turn`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#run_turn)
attaches every `@path` it names.

Three commands are handled by the surface itself before anything else:
`/theme NAME` switches palette for the session and repaints with
`apply_theme`, `/theme NAME --save` also writes `theme` under `[cli]` in
config.toml with
[`set_table`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/setup.html#set_table),
which keeps the file’s comments and other keys, `/theme` alone lists the
palettes with `list_themes`, `/root` lists the open folders and
`/root add PATH` opens another with `open_root`, and `/pane` opens or
closes the `now` pane, described at the end of this page.

### Ui.stop

``` python
def stop():
```

*Escalate repeated Ctrl-C from cancellation to termination to exit.*

`stop` is what `ctrl+c` does, and repeated presses escalate. During a
turn, the first press cancels the turn’s run, the second terminates it,
and the third quits; presses count as repeats only while they come
within the agent’s `cancel_grace` seconds of each other. Each press also
takes queued lines back into the composer, so nothing you typed is lost.

For a `!` command, `stop` signals the command’s process group. The first
`ctrl+c` sends `SIGINT`, and the next sends `SIGKILL`, however long
after the first it comes. A command ended by a signal prints `stopped`,
and the prompt is free once the process exits. Quitting kills a command
that is still running.

`on_key` is patched once more so that `ctrl+c` stops a turn without
clearing the composer, and `alt+up` pulls queued text back into the
composer for editing.

``` python
import tempfile
```

``` python
armed = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'armed'
sh_ui.buf.insert(f"!trap '' INT; touch {armed}; sleep 30")
sh_ui.start_turn(sh_ui.submit())
sh_running = sh_ui.turn
for _ in range(100):   # SIGINT before the trap is set would end the shell, so wait until it is
    if armed.exists(): break
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
assert armed.exists()
sh_ui.stop()
await asyncio.sleep(0.6)   # longer than `cancel_grace`, and the command ignores SIGINT
test_eq(sh_running.done(), False)
sh_ui.stop()
await asyncio.wait_for(sh_running, 5)
sh_comp.stop()
test_eq((sh_ui.turn, sh_ui.shell_proc), (None, None))
sh_last = sh_ui.transcript.block_text(list(sh_comp.blocks.values())[-1])
assert 'stopped' in sh_last, [sh_ui.transcript.block_text(b) for b in list(sh_comp.blocks.values())[-4:]]
sh_last
```

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ramabana/blob/main/ramabana/cli.py#L3413"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python

    k

```

*Ctrl-C stops without wiping the composer; alt+up pulls queued text back
into it; `?` on an empty composer prints the key card; `TASKS_KEY` lists
the background tasks.*

``` python
class _StopAgent:
    cancel_grace = 1
    def __init__(self):
        self.r = type('R', (), {'id': 'r1', 'terminal': False})()
    def run(self, run_id=''): return self.r
    def cancel(self, run_id): self.r.terminal = True; return {'state': 'detached'}
    def terminate(self, run_id): return {'state': 'terminated'}
    def leftovers(self): return []

class _StopUi:
    mark_read = Ui.mark_read
    def __init__(self):
        self.agent, self._stop_at, self._stop_count, self._stop_run = _StopAgent(), 0., 0, ''
        self.notes, self.turn, self.starting, self.shell_proc = [], None, False, None
        self._queued = None
        self._steered = []
    def note(self, text): self.notes.append(text)
    def take_back(self): return Ui.take_back(self)
    def paint(self): return None
    def _post(self, fn, *a): return fn(*a)

u = _StopUi()
Ui.stop(u); time.sleep(.02)
Ui.stop(u); time.sleep(.02)
test_eq(u.notes[:4], ['cancelling', 'detached', 'terminating', 'terminated'])
test_eq(Ui.stop(u), 'quit')
```

## The `now` pane

The `now` pane is a small live view, in a tmux split beside the chat, of
what the main agent and each sub-agent are doing at this moment: the
turn, the call it is on, and each sub-agent run with its own calls. The
surface writes a snapshot,
[`now_snapshot`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#now_snapshot),
to `<runs_dir>/now.json` from its own loop: at most every `PANE_EVERY`
seconds while calls change or a turn runs, and once more when the turn
ends. `ramabana-pane`, from [pane](18_pane.ipynb), reads that file and
draws it.

- `/pane` opens it with `open_pane` and `/pane off` closes it with
  `close_pane`.
- `--pane auto|on|off` decides whether a session starts with it, through
  `start_pane`; `auto` opens it only inside tmux.
- [`pane_cmd`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#pane_cmd)
  is the shell line that runs the viewer for a given file.

When the viewer crashes rather than quits, the surface reopens it, a
limited number of times.

### pane_cmd

``` python
def pane_cmd(
    path
):
```

*The shell line that draws the `now` pane for `path`.*

``` python
import tempfile
from ramabana.pane import read_snapshot

class _Pane:
    def __init__(self, id): self.id, self.killed, self.dead = id, False, False
    def kill(self): self.killed = True
    def refresh(self): return self

class _Me:
    def __init__(self): self.splits = []
    def split(self, where, cmd, size=None): self.splits.append((where, cmd, size)); return _Pane('%9')

pane_tty = EmuTty(72, 14)
pane_comp = Compositor(pane_tty)
pane_comp._register_signals = lambda: None
await pane_comp.start()
pane_ui = Ui(pane_comp, fake_agent(cfg=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()))[0])
now = pane_ui.agent.runs_dir/'now.json'
act = pane_ui.agent.activity.start('read_file', {'path': 'a.py'})
at = pane_ui._now_at
pane_ui.agent.activity.finish(act, 'ok')
test_eq(pane_ui._now_at, at)
assert read_snapshot(now)['root']['current'].startswith('read_file'), 'the write the call started made'
pane_ui.write_now(force=True)
assert pane_ui._now_at > at and read_snapshot(now)['root']['current'] == ''

me = pane_ui.agent.host.tmux_pane = _Me()
pane_ui.open_pane()
test_eq(me.splits, [('right', pane_cmd(now), '35%')])
pane_ui.open_pane()
test_eq(len(me.splits), 1)
test_eq(pane_ui.close_pane(), 'closed the pane %9')
assert pane_ui.pane is None
pane_tty.close()
```

## Peers

Each terminal session listens on a control socket from
`ramabana.control`, so another session can steer it, prompt it and read
its events.
[`amain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#amain) starts
it with
[`start_control`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#start_control)
once the [`Ui`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#ui)
exists, and closes it however the session ends. The session writes its
events to `EVENT_FILE` in its run folder, where `events` reads them, and
its agent gets the `peers` and
[`tell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/peers.html#tell) tools.

[`UiControl`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#uicontrol)
keeps one owner of the turn. A peer’s `prompt` goes to the event loop
and through `start_turn`, as a typed line does: it starts a turn, or it
waits behind the running one in the queue and joins a line already
waiting there. The transcript shows it as from a peer. A peer’s `cancel`
is `stop`, which ctrl+c calls, so the lines waiting behind the turn come
back to the composer and nothing is lost. `status` reports the
[`Ui`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#ui)’s turn and
queue.

The user reaches other sessions too. `/peers` lists them, numbered, the
most recently active first, with no run ids. `/tell N TEXT` steers
session N of that list, and `/tell N --prompt TEXT` starts or queues a
turn there. `/tell N` alone aims the lines typed next at that session,
as `/talk` does for a sub-agent, until `/tell` or `/tell main`. What the
user sends this way asks for no approval, since the user typed it. A
`/tell` whose first word is neither a number,
[`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main) nor a
listed session id is the agent’s own `/tell RUN TEXT` to a sub-agent.

## Background tasks

`ctrl+l` (`TASKS_KEY`) and `/tasks` open a list of what runs outside the
turn: background sub-agents, `run_shell_bg` shells and folder watches.
The rows come from
[`background_rows`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#background_rows)
in `ramabana.pane`, the same source the `now` pane reads. A
[`TaskMenu`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#taskmenu)
builds them again at every draw, running tasks first and finished ones
after, so state and age stay current. Enter opens a row, `x` then `y`
stops it, and `escape` returns to the composer with its text intact.

Here the source is a fixed list, and the clock stands 125 seconds after
the shell started:

``` python
task_rows = [dict(kind='delegate', id='run_ab12', label='what does a.py define?', state='completed', elapsed=41.0, started=900.0, detail=''),
             dict(kind='shell', id='cmd_1234abcd', label='pytest -x tests', state='running', elapsed=None, started=1000.0, detail='', log=''),
             dict(kind='watch', id='fw_9c1d', label='/proj', state='watching', elapsed=None, started=None, detail='')]
task_menu = TaskMenu(lambda: task_rows, now=lambda: 1125.0)
test_eq([r['kind'] for r in task_menu.rows], ['shell', 'watch', 'delegate'])
Text('\n').join(task_menu.render()).plain
```

## Tips

While a turn runs, one grey `tip:` row ends the working rows. The tip is
`TIPS[(turn_no - 1) % len(TIPS)]`, so it stays for the whole turn and
the next turn shows the next one. No tip shows while you type, while an
approval or a menu is open, or in calm mode. `tips = false` under
`[cli]` in config.toml, `--no-tips` or `/tips off` turns it off, and
`/tips off --save` keeps that choice. Every tip names a key or command
that `HELP` lists.

``` python
TIPS[:3]
```

## Composer controls

`shift+enter` starts a new line in the message and `enter` sends it.
`ctrl+a` selects the whole message, and the next typed key replaces the
selection. The example feeds the bytes a terminal sends: a kitty
`shift+enter` between two words, then `ctrl+a`.

``` python
cm_tty = EmuTty(72, 14)
cm_comp = Compositor(cm_tty)
cm_comp._register_signals = lambda: None
await cm_comp.start()
